messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: p99 latency > 1.2s (EU-west) on route /generate for model rdx-large. Alert ID: A-1771234567. Auto-page to oncall.
PagerDuty: Pager A-1771234567 fired and sent to schedule 'eng-oncall-eu'.
Anya (oncall): Acked. Looking. :eyes:
Mike O: seeing the same on dashboards — p95 ~700ms, p99 spiking 1.3-1.6s on EU-west. Requests backing up at tokenizer.
Anya (oncall): Any recent deploys?
Devindra: No deploys in EU-west since 02:00 UTC. Only config change was autoscaler tuning yesterday.
SRE Lead: Can someone run quick tail of logs for tokenization queue errors? `kubectl logs -l app=tokenizer -n inference --since=10m`
Mike O: grabbing logs.
Mike O: ```
2026-03-15T10:11:23Z tokenizer-1 WARN queue_size=124 latency_ms=1200
2026-03-15T10:11:25Z tokenizer-2 WARN kvcache-miss hotkey user:tokkey-42
2026-03-15T10:11:28Z tokenizer-1 ERROR backpressure activated
```
Anya (oncall): hotkey detected, KV cache miss + backpressure. Could be hot user or prefix. Any customer impact reports?
Customer Success: Some customers reported timeouts in their dashboards around 10:10 UTC, one ticket open (CS-2891). Not widespread but correlated.
Devindra: I'm seeing a surge of a small subset of keys — likely an automated eval job hammering. Rate from a single API token looks high. Querying logs: `select count(*) from requests where token_id='tk_ev1' and region='eu-west' and time > now() - 10m` returning 9k.
Anya (oncall): Nice catch. If it's one token, we can throttle or block to recover. Can we find token owner?
Devindra: Mapping... owner is `ci-eval@partnercorp` (internal mapping).
SRE Lead: Recommend temporary key rotation or throttling via the rate-limiter: `rlctl ban --token tk_ev1 --duration 10m`
Anya (oncall): Doing that now.
Anya (oncall): `rlctl ban --token tk_ev1 --duration 10m` -> accepted. PagerDuty: ack recorded.
incident-bot: Action recorded: token ban applied by Anya (oncall).
Mike O: p99 dropping to ~950ms within 60s. p95 unchanged but queue sizes decreasing.
Anya (oncall): Good. We'll keep monitoring 10m window. Can we also warm KV cache for the affected keys to avoid repeated misses?
Devindra: We can prime the KV cache for the hot prefixes: `kvtool warm --keys tokkey-42 --region eu-west` but that may not help if the pattern is high-cardinality.
SRE Lead: If it's truly a single token, throttling should be sufficient. Also consider adding a transient rule on router to route this token to lower-priority tier to protect tail latency.
Anya (oncall): Agree. I'll open a short-lived routing rule. `routerctl route --token tk_ev1 --tier low-priority --ttl 15m`
Anya (oncall): Rule applied.
Customer Success: CS notified the affected customer and told them we're mitigating. They replied they were running an internal load test and will pause.
PagerDuty: Paging escalation suppressed (manual override) as incident is acknowledged and declining.
Mike O: Observability shows CPU on tokenizer nodes peaked then trending down. No OOMs, no GPU preemptions.
Anya (oncall): Rolling restart not required. We'll leave throttles and routing rule for 15m then reassess.
Devindra: Leaving the warm job queued but hold off — might flood the cache.
SRE Lead: Action items: 1) follow-up with partnercorp to ask why eval ran uncontrolled. 2) Add alerting for single-token high-rate anomalies. 3) Postmortem if this repeats.
Anya (oncall): I'll hand off to Mike for monitoring and post-incident notes. Handoff: `Anya -> Mike O` oncall at 10:16 UTC.
Mike O: Taking over. I'll watch for re-trigger and coordinate with CS.
Customer Success: Customer paused their run. We'll confirm no further impact.
Anya (oncall): Thanks team. Closing page if no more spikes in 10m.
incident-bot: Incident note: mitigation applied (token throttled, routing rule), metrics trending down. Auto-close window started (10m).
Mike O: 10m check-in: stable. p99 ~480-600ms. No new pages.
Mike O: I'll create tracking ticket OPS-4321 with timeline and assign follow-up to Devindra for anomaly alerting and to CS for customer outreach.
SRE Lead: Add temporary SLO note for today to mark this as customer-impacting but isolated.
Devindra: Also propose a quick guardrail: if single-token > 5k reqs in 5m, auto-throttle at 200 rps. I'll draft a change.
Customer Success: Marking CS-2891 resolved (customer confirmed pause).
Anya (oncall): Closing the thread. Thanks. :white_check_mark: 
Mike O: Postmortem draft: will include timeline, root cause (uncontrolled eval token), mitigations (token throttled, routing tier), and actions (anomaly alert, token rate guardrail).
